End use effective rate The end use effective rate, expressed in $/kWh, represents the cost of fueling a given end use. It is calculated as a weighted average of the hourly price profile, weighted by the end use load in each hour. The end use effective rate can be calculated for the baseline load profile as well as the new load profile after price response. From there, fractional or absolute savings on the rate can be explored, and absolute rates can be compared across price and response scenarios. Unlike absolute bill impacts, the end use effective rate metric would be complicated by the presence of subscriptions; the allocation of the subscription bill across end uses would not be straightforward due to the nonlinear nature of otherwise applicable tariffs (fixed charges, demand charges, tiered rates, etc.). This means that end uses that have more coincident peak load (i.e., cooling) and can respond to prices in these peak hours, are expected to have the most significant effective shed results, whereas space heating is unlikely to contribute any effective shed, even if made completely flexible, because there is no load occurring in the hours when the system net load is peaking.
